1.0.s.en: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

1.0.0.en: In the beginning: that is, the beginning of the creation of the world, and not eternity as is meant in (Jn 1:1). It is not a specific time, for there was no time then, but it announces the beginning of the world, which only God knows, who alone was present at that time, and God has not revealed it to man. Before it was eternity, and no creatures existed before that, whether heavenly or earthly. Created: this means that God is the Creator of the world out of nothing, and this is against the theory of the eternity of the world that some philosophers proclaim.

1.0.1.en: God: in the Hebrew language it came as "Elohim", that is, in the plural, and it means God, the Trinity of hypostases, although the word "created" came in Hebrew in the singular. The meaning of this is that the one God, the Trinity of hypostases, is the One who created the world. Heavens: this means everything that is above man, that is, the world of spirits with all the orders of angels and all the heavens with their different degrees.

1.0.2.en: The earth: this means the visible world, and it includes the dry land, the seas and all perceptible beings.

1.0.3.en: This verse declares that God alone is the Creator of the world and of all that is in it.

1.1.0.en: Without form and void: in Hebrew, desolation and confusion, and in Greek in the Septuagint, invisible and unfinished. It means that obscurity and incompleteness surrounded the earth, and it was invisible because man had not yet been created. It does not mean that some being had caused confusion in it, but rather incompleteness and the absence of life in it, because God had not yet created the world in its known form, which He made for the life of man. The deep: that is, waters covering everything, so that no land could be seen in them, nor any planets or sun.

1.1.1.en: Darkness: this means a very thick fog that prevents sight, making everything vague and obscure.

1.1.2.en: The Spirit of God: the Holy Spirit, for it is a clear declaration of the Third Hypostasis.

1.1.3.en: Moved: that is, moved, and the Syriac word means "brooded", that is, hope is hung on the Spirit of God, who is able to give life out of this ruin and emptiness.

1.1.4.en: It declares to us that God created out of nothing, as we understand from (v. 1), the beginnings of the heavens and the earth, which are this water and the thick fog that covers the earth and all the planets, and the Spirit of God was brooding over this creation in which He would give life, in this water and the earth hidden within it.

1.2.0.en: How did light precede the creation of the sun, which came on the fourth day?!

1.2.1.en: The light meant here is the creation of the cosmic galaxies, each of which carries millions of stars and hundreds of millions of planets, and every planet and every star and every galaxy is in a state of rotation about itself at a very high speed. This whole cosmic entity (the galaxies) and what lies between them was called light, and it is an entity of light that preceded the appearance of the sun that we know ... The greatest proof of the existence of light apart from the sun is that scientists are now able to see and identify the galaxies, which could not be seen if they were dark. As for the sun that we know, either it existed on the first day but in a gaseous, cosmic, foggy state and completed its maturity and appearance on the fourth day, or it was taken from the luminous mass on the fourth day. This accords with science and does not contradict it, and it is the opinion supported by His Holiness Pope Shenouda III in his book "Years with People's Questions", Part One, and by His Grace Anba Paula, Bishop of Gharbia, in his book "The Bible and Science."

1.3.0.en: God declares His satisfaction with the light that He created by describing it as good, that is, it fulfilled the will of God, and this is an important first step before the creation of the other things for the sake of man.

1.3.1.en: He divided the light from the darkness: that is, there came to be an illuminated region, which is the region of the nebula and the cosmic galaxies, and another region, which is the darkness from which the created light came forth. In a spiritual contemplation, St. Augustine sees that this darkness means the fall of the angels who became demons, so God divided between the light and the darkness, that is, between the angels and the demons.

1.4.0.en: God gave the light the name Day, while the darkness He called Night. This day is different from the day produced by the sun, which means specific hours, as it will begin on the fourth day, but a day with God is a period of time not known, which may include millions of years by the reckoning now known.

1.4.1.en: He declared the end of the day by the presence of an evening and then a morning following it, because the darkness existed first and then God created the light, although we are accustomed to the day beginning with the morning and then the evening, but some peoples, such as the Jews, begin the day with the evening and then the morning.

1.4.2.en: The evening is meant to be the dimness, that is, weak light, and not the night that occurs after sunset, because the sun had not yet been created. For God works in the morning and the daytime.

1.4.3.en: The mention of the evening and then the morning gives a good hope that every darkness is followed by light.

1.4.4.en: The Spirit of God who dwells in you, however confused or ruined or far from God you may be because of your preoccupations and your sins, is able to work in you and create a life of light within you. So submit to Him when He guides you to every spiritual work, and your life will change and you will find the salvation of your soul.

1.5.s.en: (2) The second day: the creation of the heaven

1.5.0.en: The firmament: the earth was in a state of boiling, as scientists say, and then it calmed and its heat decreased in its outer crust, so the vapors surrounding it became cool. This envelope of air surrounding the earth is what is called the firmament, and the birds fly in it.

1.5.1.en: On the second day God created the air surrounding the globe of the earth, and it divides between waters below it, which are the waters of the seas and rivers, and other waters above it, which are the clouds that move, then condense and fall to the earth as rain, then the water evaporates from the earth to turn into clouds.

1.6.0.en: God called this air heaven, and it is the first heaven, that is, the heaven of the birds and not the heaven of the planets. Then He declares the end of the day, which is a period of time whose length is not known, as we mentioned, and the evening came, that is, the dimness, and it was followed by a morning, the beginning of a new day.

1.6.1.en: It is not mentioned that God saw what He had made on the second day to be good, as with the other days, because it is connected with and completed by what He did on the third day, when He made the dry land appear in the midst of the seas, and then after His creating the plants, also on the third day, He said that what He had made was good for the second time.

1.6.2.en: The creation of the heaven declares the existence of that which is lofty and high above the earth, to draw your gaze from the passing earthly things to the abiding heavenly things. This heaven is the beginning of other heavens, the last and highest of which is the Kingdom, that is, the everlasting existence with God. So let your goal be to reach heaven, and whenever you lift your eyes to heaven, your heart is drawn to contemplate God and to strive to please Him, so that you may have constant enjoyment with Him in eternity.

1.7.s.en: (3) The third day: the creation of the earth and the plants

1.7.0.en: The waters covered the whole earth, then cracks occurred in the earth's crust, and channels for the seas were formed, connected with one another, and the dry land appeared, raised above the seas and even bearing high mountains. Thus a place appeared where man could live, which is the dry land, while the seas he uses for traveling from one place to another on the land. He called the dry land earth and the gathering together of the waters seas, and this is a completion of what He did on the second day, and He saw that it was good, that is, He was pleased with it.

1.8.0.en: Grass: what is meant is the simple marine plants, which are the algae that appeared on the sides of the sea.

1.8.1.en: Herb: these are the plants of the various crops such as wheat and beans ... which give food to man and animals.

1.8.2.en: Yielding seed: it differs from the previous grasses, which are the algae, in that it forms seeds that fall into the earth and produce new plants of the same kind as the plant that produced these seeds.

1.8.3.en: Tree: these are all kinds of trees, small and large, that give fruit for the food of man and animals and produce seeds like the herbs, which can be planted to give the same kind of trees that produced them. Thus these plants do not perish when man or animals eat them, but their existence is renewed by means of the seeds. After the appearance of the earth, God created upon it the various plants to be food for man and the animals that serve him, and gave them the ability to multiply and continue by means of the seeds that they produce, and God saw that it was good. The repetition of the word good twice on the third day shows that the first is connected with what He did on the second day, as we mentioned.

1.9.0.en: God's work on the third day ends with the coming of the evening, which is followed by the morning of the fourth day.

1.9.1.en: God's love formed for you a place on which to settle, and He set bounds for the sea so that it would not overwhelm you and destroy you, then He gave you plants of many kinds to eat from as you wish. It is a love and care that surpass man's understanding, and God awaits you to settle in Him and be satisfied with His love. All these gifts are meant to draw your heart to Him and to let you see Him in them. When you walk on the earth you feel Him carrying you, and when you eat the plants you feel His hand feeding you, so you rejoice in His love and are eager to thank Him night and day.

1.10.s.en: (4) The fourth day: the creation of the sun, the moon and the stars

1.10.0.en: Lights: these are the stars, the most important of which is the sun.

1.10.1.en: In the firmament of the heaven: what is meant by it is the heaven of the planets, and not the heaven of the birds, which was created previously on the second day.

1.10.2.en: Day and night: as a result of the earth's rotation around the sun, the day came to be with its two parts, day and night, and thus the time now known began on the fourth day, which is the day that comprises 24 hours. Signs: divine wonders in the rotation of the earth, the sun, the planets and the various stars in set courses.

1.10.3.en: Seasons: the time now known began.

1.10.4.en: Days: the plural of day, which includes the day and the night.

1.10.5.en: Years: the year, which includes the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.

1.10.6.en: On the fourth day God created and ordered the sun, the moon and the stars together with the earth and the rest of the planets, and by this He formed time with its different periods, whether over the course of the year with its four seasons or over the course of the day with its two parts, night and day.

1.11.0.en: What is meant by the sun, the moon and the stars is that they give light upon the earth, so they are for its service or the service of man.

1.12.1.en: To rule the day: to order and serve the day by shining upon the earth, announcing the hours of the day and providing the sight and the heat needed for man's work.

1.12.3.en: To rule the night: to order the night and its hours and the lighting in it, together with the rest of the stars.

1.12.4.en: God created the sun, the moon and the stars to order the day and the night on the earth, so that the day would be suitable for man's work and the night for his rest, so that he regains his energy for work on the following day. The sun is a type of Christ, the Sun of righteousness, and the moon of the Church, because she receives her light, like the moon, by the reflection upon her of the light of the sun, that is, Christ. As for the stars, they are types of the saints, because they are exalted above earthly things and give light to the people after them until they complete their striving and reach heaven.

1.13.0.en: God created all these heavenly bodies in the heaven of the planets to order the day and the night. God was pleased with what He had made and testified that it was good, and thus the work of creation on the fourth day ended, and the evening came, followed by the morning of the fifth day.

1.13.1.en: Would that you make use of the divine order of day and night, working with energy in the day, using the time faithfully for doing good and showing your faithfulness to God and your love for those around you, while at night you grow quiet with yourself to pray to God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

1.14.s.en: (5) The fifth day: the creation of the sea creatures and the birds

1.14.0.en: Creeping things: this includes all kinds of fish and sea creatures that live within the sea, such as the whale, or that creep to come out onto the land at times, such as the crocodile and the seal.

1.14.1.en: Living soul: it gives them movement, vitality and instincts, but it is not the human spirit. In the open firmament of heaven: that is, in the air surrounding the earth.

1.14.2.en: On the fifth day God created all kinds of sea creatures, so the sea was filled with them, and likewise He filled the air with birds that can walk on the earth and fly in the air, whether large or small birds, some of which incline to life on the earth, such as poultry, and some of which settle on trees, mountains and high places.

1.15.0.en: Great whales: what is meant by them is the large sea creatures such as the whale, and most of these huge sea creatures have become extinct.

1.15.1.en: God created different kinds of sea creatures and likewise of birds.

1.16.0.en: God gave the sea creatures and the birds the ability to multiply and reproduce, to preserve their kinds and to increase until they fill the sea, the air and the earth.

1.17.0.en: The creation of the fifth day ended, and the evening came, followed by the morning of the sixth day.

1.17.1.en: The Christian is likened to the fish that can swim against the current, that is, does not submit to the evil thoughts of the world, and is also likened to the bird that tends to rise toward heaven. Would that you imitate these creatures in looking to God and holding fast to His commandments even if those around you reject them, and incline to prayer and the love of contemplating God.

1.18.s.en: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

1.18.0.en: Living creatures: the higher animals that live on the earth, which are other than the sea creatures and the birds.

1.18.1.en: After his kind: that is, each kind of animal is different from the other, and God created of it a male and a female to produce animals of their same kind and species.

1.18.2.en: Cattle: the tame animals such as the livestock used in farming.

1.18.3.en: Creeping thing: all the four-footed animals that move along on the earth.

1.18.4.en: Beast of the earth: the animals that became predatory after the Fall.

1.18.5.en: On the sixth day God created all kinds of animals that live on the earth.

1.19.0.en: After God created the animals, He was pleased with what He had made and declared that it was good.

1.20.0.en: Let us make: He speaks here in the plural to declare His Holy Trinity, who carried out the creation of the whole world, and He mentions it here because this is the most important work, the creation of man.

1.20.1.en: Our image: the image of God, not in the body but in the spirit, by which man is distinguished from the rest of creatures, and which includes the mind and the emotion.

1.20.2.en: After our likeness: that is, the inclination to be like God and to imitate Him.

1.20.3.en: Let them have dominion: He means man, who will multiply, and will lead, manage and tend all the animals.

1.20.4.en: After the creation of the animals on the sixth day, God created the greatest being, who is man, and this means that He brought him into being out of nothing, and that he is not one who spontaneously evolved from lower animals. He created him distinguished from the rest of creatures by the presence of a spirit in him, so that he becomes in the image and likeness of God, and He also gave him to be a leader and to have dominion over all kinds of animals.

1.21.0.en: He declares here that He created man male and female, and this is what He will explain in detail in (ch. 2).

1.22.0.en: God gave man the blessing to multiply, fill the earth and have dominion over all the animals, and this is God's plan and has no relation to man's fall. He could multiply without falling, and therefore the sexual relationship has no connection with sin, but is a relationship blessed by God for bearing fruit and filling the earth. He said "blessed them" because He means in Adam and Eve the whole human race.

1.23.0.en: God gave the plants to be food for man, and afterward, after the Fall, He gave him to eat the herb like the animals (ch. 3:18), while as for the animals, He permitted him to eat them after the Flood (ch. 9:3). It is noted that He gave him the superior plants, which are the herb and the fruits of the trees, that is, the well-known crops of the field and the fruits of the orchard.

1.24.0.en: As for the animals, God gave them the plants also to eat and live by, but the lower plants, which are the grasses that include the algae and the various weeds and some of the plants cultivated in the field.

1.25.0.en: After the creation of man God testifies that what He had made is very good, distinguishing him from the rest of the creatures of the world, because the goal of creation is man, so that the whole world might be at his service, and with this the sixth day ends. It is noted that if man was created on the sixth day, he was also renewed and redeemed on the sixth day, that is, on Great Friday and at the sixth hour, by the crucifixion of Christ.

1.25.1.en: The goal of your creation is that you imitate God and grow toward Him, and the whole world is under your feet, to use it to reach God. So do not become preoccupied with it at the expense of your goal, but seek God in everything you see of creatures and thank Him for all His gifts, and you will feel His fellowship on earth until you reach your permanent place with Him in the Kingdom. Adam and Eve in Paradise
